Why go: a slow day on a Thai fishing boat

This is a private day on a traditional wooden boat with a local crew, mixing trolling and line fishing with a snorkel at Koh Tan and lunch on board. It is relaxed rather than competitive, and honest about it: the Gulf of Thailand around Samui is shallow, so catches are modest coastal fish. If you want a sociable, unhurried day at sea with your own boat, it is excellent value for a group.

What you'll do

After pickup you board on the south coast and troll along the shore towards Koh Tan, where the boat anchors for snorkelling over the reef and a Thai lunch or BBQ. In the afternoon you can visit Koh Madsum (Pig Island) before more line fishing on the way back to the pier.

Who it suits

  • Families and groups of friends who want their own boat for a day.
  • Beginners and children trying fishing for the first time.
  • Groups of 8–11, where the per-person cost is low for a private boat.

Who should choose something else

  • Serious anglers after big game: you need a deep-water trip towards Koh Tao or beyond. See our fishing guide.
  • Snorkellers who mainly want reefs and Pig Island: the private longtail or private speedboat is quicker.

Good to know

  • Conservation: the crew releases small fish; please don't keep more than you can eat.
  • Seasickness: wooden boats roll more than speedboats when stopped; take a tablet before you leave if you are prone.
  • Weather: October to December brings the strongest winds and the most cancellations.

Before you book

Pick the price band for your group size, including children. Tell us if anyone is a keen angler, so the crew brings suitable tackle, and whether you want the Pig Island stop. Bring a cool box with ice if you hope to take fish back to a villa kitchen.
